title: Filter shipments by pasted tracking reference and by carrier

blocks.text: The shipment desk pastes tracking references from carrier e-mails into a form. A reference is two capital letters, nine digits and two capital letters, and the pattern is already in `TRACKING_REF`. Anything else goes back to the sender for correction, because the carrier's tracking API rejects it a day later. The desk also lists shipments by carrier; a shipment with a `null` carrier hasn't been handed to one yet, and the desk asks for those by passing `null`.

Write `validRef()` and `byCarrier(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Shipments.java`. A pasted text is valid only if it is a reference and nothing else. The carrier filter must work for every carrier, `null` included, on a list where some shipments have no carrier. About two lines in total.

cases.says: references with too few digits, lower-case letters or no letters are sent back; well-formed ones are not
when every shipment has a carrier, the filter lists exactly the named carrier's shipments
a well-formed reference with other text before or after it is sent back
a well-formed reference followed by a line break is sent back
asking for the null carrier lists the shipments not handed over yet
a carrier's shipments are listed even when some shipments have no carrier

origin.section: Predicate.isEqual Is Null-Safe on Both Sides; equals Called Through a Lambda Is Not

concepts: Pattern.asPredicate tests find(), so it accepts input with the pattern anywhere in it; asMatchPredicate tests matches(), the whole input, and ^...$ with asPredicate still accepts a trailing line terminator.
Predicate.isEqual tests Objects.equals, so a null target or a null element is a value; c.equals(w) throws at a null element and w::equals throws when created with a null w.
